analysis: Testosterone, a primary male sex hormone, is predominantly produced by the Leydig cells, which are located in the testes. These cells are specifically responsible for the synthesis of testosterone in response to luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary gland. The other options listed do not primarily contribute to testosterone production.
